name: Gods Without Worshippers: The Beliefs People Left Behind
description: Osiris, Zeus, Odin and Huitzilopochtli once ruled the lives of millions. Follow the lost religions, and the scripts and calendars that carried them, from the temple to the ruin.

checkpoints.name: The first gods
checkpoints.note: In the river valleys of Iraq and Egypt, priests build the first great temples, record prayers in cuneiform and hieroglyphs, and count the year by the flood and the stars.

checkpoints.name: Pantheons of the classical world
checkpoints.note: Greeks, Romans, Celts and Etruscans honour crowds of gods with festivals, oracles and sacrifices. Rome borrows freely from every people it meets, and the old calendars keep time for all of them.

checkpoints.name: The old gods fade
checkpoints.note: Mithras, Mani and Odin win followers in turn, but emperors and kings who choose Christianity or Islam close temples and ban rites. By the end of this age most of the old worship is gone from Europe and the Near East.

checkpoints.name: Gods of the Americas
checkpoints.note: In Mexico and the Andes, the Aztec and Inca states give religion a central place in public life. Spanish conquest ends their state cults, but the Maya scripts and calendars survive to be read again.
